title: Wall-Mounted Swing-Jib Crane for Battery-Pack Handling
summary: Battery-pack handling: independent idealization followed by a supplied numerical model, signed equilibrium, nominal stress and displacement checks, and an evidence-limited engineering assessment.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor-only signed free bodies of the pinned boom, axial brace, wall supports and hypothetical C pin/lug; reference arrows define positive axes.
problemStatement:
You are studying a wall-mounted swing-jib crane concept for repeated battery-pack handling at an automotive workstation. The concept illustration shows a boom, a lower diagonal brace, a trolley/hoist and a suspended load. Use it to discuss function, material choices, load paths and missing design evidence. It is a context illustration, not a measured installation or a definition of the numerical model.

First develop your own structural idealization and free-body diagrams in task I1. State the restraints, load transfer and omitted effects you assume. Different defensible idealizations may be proposed at this stage.
engineeringGoal: Develop and assess a limited instructional model, distinguish assigned nominal criteria from unverified physical capacities, and identify the engineering evidence needed before a real lifting system could be approved.
commonModelStatement:
For tasks M1–M5, use the separately supplied common model after I1. The boom has an ideal in-plane wall pin at A, is continuous through the brace attachment C, and extends to D. The lower brace anchor B and A are fixed points in a rigid wall. A is vertically above B; C is a horizontal distance a from A; D is a horizontal distance L from A. The brace angle theta is measured from horizontal, so wall-anchor separation is h = a tan(theta) and physical brace length is ell_b = a/cos(theta).

Move the payload to D at full reach for the assigned numerical case. Apply downward P = gamma_d M g at D. Analyze both prescribed horizontal directions H_x = +H and H_x = −H, with equivalent boom couple C_e = H_x e_H, positive counterclockwise. This force/couple pair is an idealized boom loading; it is not a moment transmitted through the freely suspended chain shown in the context illustration.

Calculate first-order equilibrium, nominal stresses and the braced tip displacement using boom bending and brace axial deformation. Neglect boom axial compliance, shear deformation, connection clearance, wall flexibility and geometric nonlinearities. Other equipment and structural weights are omitted. These assumptions bound the exercise and do not establish an actual crane response.

All provided dimensions, properties, amplification factors and comparison criteria are instructional assignments without documented industrial provenance. Compare only the specified nominal responses with their assigned criteria. A formal Euler calculation is included to examine its assumptions and section-axis ambiguity; it is not an established compression capacity. Identify unassessed modes and evidence required before an actual lifting system could be approved.
contextImageNote: Context illustration only. Historical diagonal L_b, wall-spacing H, hook-height h_0 and inboard trolley labels do not define the numerical variables or load position. The numerical model uses horizontal a = Lb and a full-reach load. Use the authoritative common model after I1. Image provenance and industrial dimensions are undocumented.
idealizedImageCaption: Instructor reference: complete signed cases; negative forces reverse reference arrows. Schematic / not to scale. Current-input tables govern.

supplementaryImages.alt: Unsolved authoritative pinned-boom/axial-brace geometry: interior and endpoint panels, prescribed load directions and hypothetical pin/lug topology.
supplementaryImages.caption: Authoritative numerical model. Panel A: a < L; panel B: a = L. Applied loads are symbolic givens; no solved forces or displacements. Schematic / not to scale.

commonModelAssumptions: A = (0,0), B = (0,-h), C = (a,0), D = (L,0), with a = Lb horizontal, h = a tan(theta), ell_b = a/cos(theta), and 0 < a <= L. At a = L, C and D coincide.
A restrains boom translations and releases in-plane rotation; its reaction moment is zero. B is a fixed-position brace pin. The boom is continuous through C with no internal beam hinge.
The brace is a bilateral straight pin-ended axial bar: positive F is compression, negative F is tension. Actual force-reversal capability and compression resistance are unverified.

The assigned payload acts at full reach D, unlike the inboard trolley in the historical image. P = gamma_d M g, g = 9.81 m/s^2. Hoist, trolley, fixture and structural weights are omitted, not physically absent.

Evaluate both prescribed cases H_x = +H, C_e = +H e_H and H_x = -H, C_e = -H e_H at D. Applied moments are counterclockwise-positive. This is an imposed boom force/couple pair, not a chain-transmitted moment.
First-order linear-elastic Euler-Bernoulli boom flexure and brace axial deformation are included. Use N, mm, MPa internally; convert metre inputs once.

Boom axial compliance, shear deformation, connection clearance, wall flexibility and geometric nonlinearities are explicitly omitted. These omissions do not establish that the computed motion bounds a real crane.
Equilibrium boom axial forces are still reported. A_boom is unavailable: M/S is a bending-only criterion and does not verify N/A +/- M/S or complete member stability.

The representative checked connection is a hypothetical brace-end main lug at C carrying |F|. n_s = 1 is single shear; n_s = 2 is symmetric equally shared double shear. Main-lug bearing area remains d_pin t_plate. Outer cheeks, pin bending and other modes are unassessed.

All properties, dimensions, loads, amplification and criteria are assigned instructional values without documented industrial provenance. Small-strain/rotation validity has no approved quantitative threshold.

Formal Euler calculations, K_brace and N_b are sensitivity/diagnostic quantities only. The supplied inertia axis and reported minimum radius are unverified; no formal result enters physical compression capacity or nominal utilization ranking.

Only five scoped nominal criteria are ranked. Physical compression resistance, combined boom stress, fatigue, out-of-plane behavior, wall/anchors, rated hardware and complete fixture safety remain unassessed. The root-fixed P-only cantilever is a separate changed-support comparison.
instructorBackground:
Component materials. Preserve the distinction between elastic stiffness, yield onset, ultimate fracture, toughness, fatigue and wear. Boom/brace section geometry and material choice must be considered together. Pins may require different material and heat treatment because bending, contact, wear and fatigue accompany nominal shear. Plates, welds and anchors require compatible material, fabrication and supporting-wall evidence. No grade or pin resistance is established by the assigned member E and yield reference.

Operational loading and geometry. A real design brief must address hoist/trolley/fixture and structural weights, acceleration, braking, impact, side pull, swing, repeated duty, clearances and workspace. The numerical battery-only case deliberately omits those unspecified actions. Distinguish system geometry, member sections/axes and local connection dimensions; do not infer a measured section or trolley travel from the illustration.

Connections and life. Nominal pin shear and main-lug bearing are only two checks. Pin bending, lug net section and tear-out, edge distance, clearance, welds, other plates, retaining hardware, wall anchors, cyclic contact and inspection remain separate engineering issues. Fatigue needs load history and appropriate detail/material evidence; proof-load procedures and hardware ratings require an approved basis. Hooks, chains, hoists and lifting fixtures should be rated and traceable, not approved from a nominal stress alone.

Assessment guidance. Credit explicit idealization, complete case-consistent FBDs, equilibrium, units, signed compatibility and justified limitations. Students must distinguish strength, stiffness, stability and life requirements. Do not credit a fictitious root couple, mixed-case reactions, a universal cantilever bound, or a formal Euler result presented as real compression capacity. Acknowledging missing evidence is part of the engineering answer.
